interactions.summary: A student says the Divine Comedy has reopened him to truths beyond a scientific-business framework, disturbed his sleep, and filled him with new moral and metaphysical questions; Jiang sharpens the testimony by asking about bodily and visionary effects.
Another student says the reading has intensified awareness of love, memory, forgotten people, and the fatigue that comes from heightened consciousness.

claims.claim: A student says close reading of the Divine Comedy makes him more open to realities beyond a scientific or business framework and feels like an encounter with a larger truth.
The same student reports sleep disturbance and intrusive imagery after reading, suggesting that Dante's visions continue operating after class ends.
Another student says the text heightens awareness of love, remembered persons, and neglected relations, while also producing unusual fatigue.

signature_moments.moment: Dante is described as a framework-changing text that makes a scientifically trained reader suspect realities beyond the closed universe he normally inhabits.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It shows the class treating the poem not just as literature but as a pressure system on modern epistemic identity.

signature_moments.moment: The poem keeps working at night as visions the reader has to wrestle with.
signature_moments.source_phrase: these visions were appearing before you
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It links textual encounter to altered perception rather than mere interpretation.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The student's name for the metaphysical surplus the Divine Comedy seems to point toward beyond ordinary professional frameworks.

chronology_notes.note: This packet opens an extended end-of-class sequence where evidence shifts from Dante's world to the class's own bodily, psychological, and spiritual responses to reading him.
